overview.text: Today's key developments highlight significant advances in AI safety, agentic coordination, and enterprise availability. Patch the Planet and Anthropic's data on using Claude for attack surface reduction demonstrate how automated security analysis and global response coordination are strengthening software defenses across open-source codebases. In biology, OpenAI, PerturbAI, and Scripps Research applied thousands of distributed AI agents to uncover promising research leads from millions of brain cells. Meanwhile, infrastructure and deployment landscapes continue to shift as OpenAI models arrive on Google Cloud, and SemiAnalysis projects massive datacenter expansion with substantial gigawatt additions slated for the near future. Researchers also released new frameworks tackling parallel reasoning in diffusion models, long-horizon terminal agent reliability, and unsupervised tool evolution for coding agents, collectively pushing the boundaries of autonomous system execution.

entries.title: Patch the Planet: global response coordination as agents uncover critical vulnerabilities
entries.summary: Patch the Planet connects security researchers, maintainers, and incident responders to help address critical vulnerabilities across open source.
entries.why: Coordinates global security researchers and maintainers to address critical open-source software vulnerabilities effectively.

entries.title: Using Claude to reduce the attack surface of code
entries.summary: Automated attack surface analysis and reduction can meaningfully improve the security of deployed software in the near term. In this post, we preview data we’ve collected from applying attack surface reduction techniques to large open-source codebases using Claude.
entries.why: Shows how automated analysis using Claude can meaningfully improve software security in large codebases.

entries.title: Using thousands of AI agents to uncover new leads in biological data
entries.summary: See how OpenAI, PerturbAI, and Scripps Research used distributed AI agents to uncover promising research leads in data from millions of brain cells.
entries.why: Demonstrates distributed AI agents uncovering biological research leads from millions of brain cells.

entries.title: Breaking Diffusion: Parallel Reasoning with Draft Refinement
entries.summary: Drafting an answer allows a reasoning model to reconsider each decision in the context of the others. Yet repeated diffusion denoising does not ensure that individually plausible token updates form a better answer together.
entries.why: Explores parallel reasoning and draft refinement to improve consistency in diffusion models.

entries.title: Event-STVG: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding for Long-Form Event Reasoning
entries.summary: Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding (STVG) aims to jointly localize a target in space and time given a natural-language query.
entries.why: Addresses spatio-temporal video grounding for complex natural-language event reasoning in long-form video.

entries.title: Harness Self-Evolution for Long-Horizon Terminal Agents
entries.summary: Long-horizon terminal agents may solve a task in one run yet fail across repeated runs. Stochastic errors can propagate through actions and context, creating a gap between capability and reliable execution.
entries.why: Tackles stochastic error propagation to bridge the gap between capability and reliable execution in terminal agents.

entries.title: Unsupervised Tool Evolution for Coding Agents in Data-Lake Analytics
entries.summary: Coding agents can answer analytical questions over a data lake by discovering, cleaning, and joining the relevant data. However, they discard this work after each question and redo it from scratch for the next one.
entries.why: Enables coding agents to retain and evolve analytical tools across questions in data-lake environments.

entries.summary: OpenAI and Google Cloud are bringing frontier models and Codex workflows to Gemini’s Model Garden, available through Google Cloud Marketplace.
entries.why: Expands enterprise access by bringing frontier models and workflows to Google Cloud Marketplace.

entries.title: FairStress: A deeper evaluation of fairness in LLM decision-making
entries.summary: FairStress is a new benchmark that reveals demographic differences in how LLMs defend and explain their decisions, even when their final choices appear fair.
entries.why: Evaluates hidden demographic biases in LLM decision defenses despite seemingly fair final choices.

entries.title: Claude Mods: Flipping the Harness Inside Out
entries.summary: Claude Mods is an early form of the Attention Interface. It flips the agent harness paradigm from the harness facing the machine, to the harness facing the human.
entries.why: Explores the Attention Interface concept by flipping the traditional agent harness paradigm toward humans.

entries.title: Anthropic Does Not Understand Why Its Draft Bill Was Unacceptable and Troubling
entries.summary: Anthony Cimino offered the closest thing to an official response we have seen on the leaked Anthropic draft bill I covered on Saturday.
entries.why: Discusses official responses and industry reactions surrounding a leaked Anthropic draft bill.
